Ex: Plants draw minerals and other nutrients from the soil.

suppress

(verb). cầm lại, nén

Ex: The medication effectively suppressed the pain.

weed

(noun). cỏ dại

Ex: The yard was overgrown with weeds.

pollinate

(verb). Thụ phấn

Ex: Bees pollinate the plants by carrying the pollen from one flower to another.

prey on

(verb). săn mồi

Ex: Hawks prey on rodents and small birds.

pest

(noun). Sâu hại

Ex: These birds provide a useful function in controlling pests.

fuel

(noun). nhiên liệu

Ex: Wood, coal, oil, petrol, and gas are all different kinds of fuel.

combination

(noun). Sự phối hợp

Ex: His treatment was a combination of surgery, radiation and drugs.

collapse

(noun). sự sụp đổ

Ex: The peace talks were on the verge of collapse.

market

(noun). thị trường

Ex: Expansion into the global market brings more risk.

carry out

(verb). tiến hành

Ex: The hospital is carrying out tests to find out what's wrong with her.

compare

(verb). so sánh

Ex: We compared the two reports carefully.

alarm

(verb). Làm cho hoảng sợ, làm cho lo lắng

Ex: It alarms me that nobody takes this problem seriously.

harness

(verb). sử dụng

Ex: There is a great deal of interest in harnessing wind and waves as new sources of power.

threaten

(verb). đe dọa

Ex: Pollution is threatening marine life.

directly

(adverb). một cách trực tiếp

Ex: He was not directly responsible for the accident.

maintain

(verb). duy trì

Ex: The two countries have always maintained close relations.

measure

(noun). Phương sách, biện pháp

Ex: The government is introducing tougher measures to combat crime.

loss

(noun). mất mát

Ex: He suffered a loss of confidence.

preservation

(noun). sự bảo quản

Ex: The council has placed a preservation order on the building.

subsistence

(noun). sinh kế, sự cầm cự

Ex: Many families are living below the level of subsistence.

virtually

(adverb). hầu như, gần như

Ex: Virtually all students will be exempt from the tax.

identical

(adjective). y hệt

Ex: Her dress is almost identical to mine. Ex: identical twins

corresponding

(adjective). tương ứng, phù hợp

Ex: A change in the money supply brings a corresponding change in expenditure.

procedure

(noun). thủ tục, thể thức

Ex: Making a complaint is quite a simple procedure.

distinguish

(verb). phân biệt

Ex: At what age are children able to distinguish between right and wrong?

survive

(verb). Sống sót, tồn tại

Ex: They spent two months in the jungle, surviving on small animals and fruit.

researcher

(noun). Nhà nghiên cứu

Ex: Researchers found there was no evidence of an increased risk of infection.

descend on

(verb). bất ngờ ồ ạt đến thăm ai/cái gì

Ex: Hundreds of football fans descended on the city.

tiny

(adjective). rất nhỏ

Ex: We come from a tiny little town in upstate New York.

astonished

(adjective). Ngạc nhiên, kinh ngạc

Ex: She was quite astonished at his rudeness.

insect

(noun). côn trùng

Ex: There are about 30 million species of insects in the world.

species

(noun). giống loài

Ex: Most of the known rhino species are West African.

forest

(noun). rừng rậm

Ex: Thousands of hectares of forest are destroyed each year.

diversity

(noun). sự đa dạng

Ex: There is a need for greater diversity and choice in education.

tropical

(adjective). thuộc về nhiệt đới

Ex: The Amazon river basin contains the world's largest tropical rainforest.

biodiversity

(noun). sự đa dạng sinh học

Ex: The mining project threatens one of the world’s richest areas of biodiversity.

hotspot

(noun). điểm nóng

Ex: Scientists refer to these areas as biological hot spots.

plantation

(noun). Đồn điền

Ex: Hundreds of slaves used to work on the plantations.

habitat

(noun). Môi trường sống

Ex: The panda's natural habitat is the bamboo forest.

wildlife

(noun). giới hữu sinh

Ex: Development of the area would endanger wildlife.

prefer

(verb). thích hơn

Ex: I much prefer jazz to rock music.

selectively

(adverb). Có chọn lọc; dựa trên sự chọn lọc

Ex: The cattle have not been selectively bred for beef or milk.

genuinely

(adverb). một cách thành thật, một cách chân thật, thật sự

Ex: There are some genuinely funny moments in the film.

sustainable

(adjective). Có thể duy trì lâu dài; Thân thiện với môi trường

Ex: This type of farming is simply not sustainable any more.

shade

(noun). bóng, bóng râm

Ex: The shade of the pine tree provided some protection from the sun.

method

(noun). Phương pháp

Ex: Which method is the most effective?

migrate

(verb). Di cư

Ex: These animals migrate annually in search of food.

refuge

(noun). Nơi trốn tránh, nơi ẩn náu, nơi trú ẩn

Ex: They were forced to seek refuge from the fighting.

vital

(adjective). thiết yếu, quan trọng

Ex: She had found out some information of vital importance.

cultivation

(noun). sự trồng trọt

Ex: The cultivation of wheat required the most fertile lands.

require

(verb). cần, yêu cầu

Ex: These pets require a lot of care and attention.

pesticide

(noun). thuốc trừ sâu

Ex: Do not pour pesticides or herbicides down sinks, drains or toilets.

fertiliser

(noun). Phân bón

Ex: Fertilizer helps to enrich the soil.

huge

(adjective). to lớn

Ex: A huge crowd had gathered in the square.

conservation

(noun). Sự bảo tồn

Ex: Road development in the area has been severely affected by the conservation programmes of the council.

research

(noun). nghiên cứu

Ex: His researches in the field of disease prevention produced unexpected results.

incentive

(noun). Động lực

Ex: There is no incentive for people to save fuel.

convert

(verb). Chuyển đổi

Ex: The hotel is going to be converted into a nursing home.

exist

(verb). Tồn tại

Ex: I don't think ghosts exist.

primary

(adjective). chính

Ex: The primary aim of this course is to improve your spoken English.

remote

(adjective). xa xôi, hẻo lánh

Ex: The area is remote, mountainous, and roadless.

steep

(adjective). Dốc đứng

Ex: The path grew steeper as we climbed higher.

encourage

(verb). khuyến khích

Ex: My parents have always encouraged me in my choice of career.

criteria

(noun). điều kiện, tiêu chuẩn

Ex: We have specific criteria and certain limitations.

process

(noun). quá trình

Ex: It's a normal part of the learning process.

rigorous

(adjective). Tỉ mỉ, kĩ càng

Ex: The second team adopted a much more rigorous approach to the problem.

gain

(noun). lợi ích

Ex: These policies have resulted in great gains in public health.

offer

(verb). Cung cấp

Ex: The hotel offers excellent facilities for families.

financial

(adjective). về mặt tài chính

Ex: She's an independent financial adviser.

rival

(verb). sánh với, cạnh tranh với

Ex: You will find scenery to rival anything you can see in the Alps.

currently

(adverb). tại thời điểm hiện tại

Ex: All the options are currently available.

cultural

(adjective). thuộc về văn hóa

Ex: Teachers need to be aware of cultural differences.

ecological

(adjective). Liên quan đến hệ sinh thái

Ex: The destruction of the rain forests is an ecological disaster.

significance

(noun). sự quan trọng, sự đáng kể

Ex: The new drug has great significance for the treatment of the disease.

cooperative

(noun). cửa hàng hợp tác xã

Ex: The family business is now run as a cooperative.

labour

(noun). lao động chân tay

Ex: Companies are making huge profits by exploiting cheap labour in poor countries.

condition

(noun). trạng thái

Ex: Many of the paintings are in poor condition.

crop

(noun). cây trồng

Ex: The crops are regularly sprayed with pesticides.

expect

(verb). mong đợi

Ex: They never expected to find their dream home.

drive

(noun). sự khao khát, động lực

Ex: We have this insatiable drive to be successful in the markets we serve.

yield

(noun). sản lượng, hoa lợi

Ex: a reduction in milk yield Ex: Organic farmers use natural controls and work with nature's cycles to produce healthful, abundant yields.

swathe

(noun). vùng đất

Ex: Development has affected vast swathes of our countryside.

intensive

(adjective). tập trung, chuyên sâu, mạnh mẽ

Ex: The course compresses two year's training into six intensive months.

monoculture

(noun). Độc canh

Ex: Extensive irrigation for corn monoculture depletes water resources.

pattern

(noun). Khuôn mẫu

Ex: Wages in both sectors have followed a similar pattern.

documentation

(noun). sự ghi chép tài liệu, giấy tờ cần thiết

Ex: No documentation to current day activity was listed.

indicate

(verb). chỉ ra, hiển thị

Ex: The survey data indicate a general satisfaction with the process.

consumer

(noun). Người tiêu dùng

Ex: Health-conscious consumers want more information about the food they buy.

certification

(noun). Sự cấp giấy chứng nhận

Ex: Additional funds are needed for training and certification of healthcare workers.

attract

(verb). thu hút

Ex: This proposal has attracted a lot of interest.

flora

(noun). hệ thực vật

Ex: The desert flora give way to oak woodlands.

fauna

(noun). hệ động vật

Ex: While she was in Hawaii, she studied the local flora and fauna.

sections.title: Passage 3: Painters of time
sections.html:
acclaim

(verb). Praise enthusiastically and publicly.

ex: The movie had won critical acclaim and is actually one of the few hits that Bollywood turned out this year so far.

throughout

(adverb). during a whole period of time.

ex: People throughout the country are out of work.

Mythology

(noun). a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

ex: this field includes archaeology, comparative mythology, and folklore

artistic

(adjective). having or revealing natural creative skill.

ex: he has exceptional artistic ability

movement

(noun). An act of moving.

ex: He made a sudden movement and frightened the bird away.

Oppression

(noun). prolonged cruel or unjust treatment or control.

ex: her mood had initially been alarm and a sense of oppression

minority

(noun). the smaller part of a group; less than half of the people or things in a large group

ex: It's only a tiny minority of people who are causing the problem.

project

(noun). An individual or collaborative enterprise that is carefully planned

ex: My next project is decorating the kitchen.

cardboard

(noun). a box made of paper to wrap up, and stock things

He was living on the streets for three months, and his home was a cardboard box.

a bolt from the blue

(phrase). something important or unusual that happens suddenly or unexpectedl

ex: His marriage proposal came like a bolt from the blue - but she said yes!

technique

(noun). A way of carrying out a particular task,

ex: We learned some techniques for relieving stress.

marketing

(noun). the action or business of promoting and selling products or services, including market research and advertising

ex: He made a career in marketing

steady

(adjective). Firmly fixed

ex: The procession moved through the streets at a steady pace.

acrylic

(adjective). a type of cloth or plastic produced by chemical processes

ex: He's wearing an acrylic scarf/sweater

wax

(noun). a solid substance containing a lot of fat that becomes soft and melts when warm

ex: She watched the wax as it dripped down the side of the candle.

guardian

(noun). a defender, protector, or keeper.

ex: The child's parents or guardians must give their consent before she has the operation.

painting

(noun). a picture that has been painted

ex: She has also done abstract paintings and made experimental films.

bark

(noun). the tough protective outer sheath of the trunk, branches, and twigs of a tree or woody shrub.

ex: beavers feed on leaves and the living bark of trees

overseas

(adverb). to or in a foreign country, especially those separated from your country by the sea or ocean

ex: We need to open up overseas markets.

commodity

(noun). a product or a raw material

ex: the international commodities market is booming

context

(noun). the circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea, and in terms of which it can be fully understood and assessed.

ex: What was the context you found the word in?

content

(adjective). In a state of peaceful happiness.

ex: I'm content to just move forward.

territory

(noun). An area of land under the jurisdiction of a ruler or state à land, boundary

ex: He was shot down in enemy territory.

unique

(adjective). being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.

ex: I'd recognize your handwriting anywhere - it's unique.

feature

(noun). a distinctive attribute or aspect of something.

ex: Our latest model of phone has several new features.

ultimate

(adjective). happening at the end of a long process

ex: My manager will make the ultimate decision about who to employ.

supreme

(adjective). of authority or an office, or someone holding it superior to all others.

ex: The board has supreme authority over such issues

region

(noun). part of a country or the world having definable characteristics

ex: There's a shortage of cheap housing in the region

dialogue

(noun). conversation between two or more people as a feature of a book, play, or movie

ex: the U.S. would enter into a direct dialogue with Vietnam

figure of speech

(phrase). a word or phrase used in a non-literal sense for rhetorical or vivid effect.

ex: "Break a leg" is a figure of speech, meaning "good luck".

infer

(verb). to reach an opinion or decide that something is true on the basis of information that is available

ex: You can infer the meaning of the word from the context of the rest of the sentence.

designate

(verb). to say officially that somebody/something has a particular character or name

ex: Traditionally, the president designates his or her successor.

exhibit

(verb). Publicly display a work of art or item of interest in an art gallery

ex: The authorities began to exhibit something of their old spirit

civilisation

(noun). a state of human society that is very developed and organized

ex: Some people think that nuclear war would mean the end of civilization.

devote

(verb). to give your time or effort completely to something you believe in or to a person, or to use a particular amount of time or energy doing something

ex: He devoted his life to serving his family, friends, and neighbors.

commission

(verb). give an order for or authorize the production of something such as a building, piece of equipment, or work of art.

ex: the portrait was commissioned by his widow in 1792

fresco

(noun). a picture made by painting on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling

ex: Michelangelo's famous frescoes are in the Sistine Chapel

immemorial

(adjective). existing or traditional for an extremely long time

ex: She said it was the immemorial custom of the villagers to have a feast after the harvesting.

internal

(adjective). connected with the inside of something

ex: He sustained injuries to his arms, legs, and several internal organs.

quest

(noun). a long or arduous search for something.

ex: Nothing will stop them in their quest for truth.

swamp

(verb). overwhelm or flood usually with water

ex: If clothes swamp you, they are much too big for you.

immigrant

(noun). A person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

ex: There is a large Indian immigrant population.

native

(adjective). An animal or plant indigenous to a place

ex: She returned to live and work in her native Japan.

undoubtedly

(adverb). without doubt; certainly.

ex: they are undoubtedly guilty

maltreat

(verb). treat a person or animal cruelly or with violence.

ex: children die from neglect or are maltreated by their carers

newcomer

(noun). a person or thing that has recently arrived in a place or joined a group

ex: she's a newcomer to the area

barren

(adjective). not good enough for plants to grow on it

ex: We drove through a barren, rocky landscape.

cram

(verb). completely fill a place or container to the point that it appears to be overflowing

ex: the ashtray by the bed was crammed with cigarette butts

slum

(noun). a squalid and overcrowded urban street or district inhabited by very poor people

ex: the area was fast becoming a slum for the destitute

outskirt

(noun). the areas that form the edge of a town or city

ex: The factory is in/on the outskirts of New Delhi.

assimilation

(noun). the process of becoming similar to something

ex: Watson was ready to work for the assimilation of Scots law to English law where he thought it was justified

integrate

(verb). Combine one thing with another to form a whole.

ex: Children are often very good at integrating into a new culture.

herd

(verb). to move together as a group, or to cause animals or people to move together in a group

ex: The teachers herded the children into buses.

nomadic

(adjective). living the life of a nomad; wandering.

ex: they absorbed the surviving nomadic descendants of the authentic autochtons.

ritual

(noun). A religious or solemn ceremony consisting of a series of actions

ex: Coffee and the newspaper are part of my morning ritual.

motif

(noun). A decorative image or design, especially a repeated one forming a pattern.

We chose some curtains with a flower motif.

collective

(adjective). Done by people acting as a group.

ex: It was Betsy who summed up our collective thoughts.

canvas

(noun). strong, rough cloth used for making tents, sails, bags, strong clothes, etc

ex: she's holding a canvas bag

astounded

(adjective). shock or greatly surprise

Ex: If he thought this scene was beautiful, he'd be astounded at her place on the mountain.

ceremonial

(noun). the system of rules and procedures to be observed at a formal or religious occasion.

ex: the procedure was conducted with all due ceremonial

missionary

(noun). a person sent on a religious mission, especially one sent to promote Christianity in a foreign country.

ex: Pearl Buck was raised in China, where her parents were Christian missionaries

reproduce

(verb). copy

ex: Sound effects can reproduce the sound of thunder.

persist

(verb). Continue in an opinion or course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

ex: If the pain persists, consult a doctor.

depict

(verb). show or represent by a drawing, painting, or other art form

The artist had depicted her lying on a bed.

synonymous

(adjective). having the same, or nearly the same, meaning

ex: The words "annoyed" and "irritated" are more or less synonymous.

cease

(verb). bring or come to an end.

ex: on his retirement the job will cease to exist

perpetuate

(verb). make something, typically an undesirable situation or an unfounded belief continue indefinitely.

ex: the law perpetuated the interests of the ruling class

religious

(adjective). relating to or believing in a religion.

ex: both men were deeply religious and intelligent

permanence

(noun). the state or quality of lasting or remaining unchanged indefinitely

ex: The establishment of these principles was essential to the integrity and permanence of the American Union.

contemporary

(adjective). Living or occurring at the same time

ex: Contemporary dancers strive to connect the mind and the body through fluid dance movements

manifestation

(noun). an event, action, or object that clearly shows or embodies something, especially a theory or an abstract idea

ex: Every word and action of his was the manifestation of an activity unknown to him

guarantee

(verb). to promise to do something

ex: The TV comes with/has a two-year guarantee.

peculiar

(adjective). strange or odd; unusual.

ex: The dog's peculiar behavior worried them.

ancestor

(noun). a person, typically one more remote than a grandparent

ex: There were portraits of his ancestors on the walls of the room.

spiritual

(adjective). relating to or affecting the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things

ex: She is a deeply spiritual person.

cooperative

(adjective). involving mutual assistance in working toward a common goal

ex: It depends how cooperative everyone is.

redistribute

(verb). distribute something differently or again, typically to achieve greater social equality.

ex: Unused federal funds will be redistributed to other states

exceptional

(adjective). unusual; not typical.

ex: He is such an exceptional boy

accompany

(verb). Be present or occur at the same time as something else

ex: She will accompany me to the store

exile

(verb). the state of being barred from one's native country, typically for political or punitive reasons

ex: The monarch was exiled because of the coup.

undeniable

(adjective). unable to be denied or disputed.

ex: Whatever the case, it was an undeniable fact now
